title: Torsion-free groups inject into their rationalization
statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group such that $m g=0$ for an integer $m>0$ implies $g=0$. The canonical homomorphism from $G$ to its rationalization $G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ [def-trf-rational-rank], $g\mapsto g\otimes 1$, is injective.

source.place: §2.1, pp. 7–8, rationalization of the ordered value group; the elementary torsion-free tensor fact is made explicit here.

proof.text: Use the positive integers S = Submonoid.pos ℤ instead of all nonzero integers. Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.FractionRing supplies IsLocalization S ℚ: every rational has a positive denominator. Thus the localization-tensor assertion [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], specialized to the base ring itself and G, identifies the canonical tensor map with module localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Mathlib packages this specialization directly as IsLocalization.tensorProduct_isLocalizedModule for f = TensorProduct.mk ℤ ℚ G 1, so no explicit comparison maps are needed. The tensor definition is [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tags 00DK and 07JZ; Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/FractionRing.lean positive-integer localization instance and Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/BaseChange.lean IsLocalization.tensorProduct_isLocalizedModule.

proof.text: If rationalizationMap G x = rationalizationMap G y, unfold only the canonical map to obtain f x = f y. By the equality criterion for module localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], implemented by IsLocalizedModule.exists_of_eq, there is m in S with m • x = m • y. In particular m is a strictly positive integer and m • (x - y) = 0 by distributivity.

source.place: Tag 07JZ, equality of fractions with denominator one.

proof.text: Apply the stated torsion-free hypothesis to the positive integer m and the group element x - y. It gives x - y = 0, hence x = y. This proves injectivity without any additional hypotheses on G.

source.place: Elementary application of the hypothesis after the Tag 07JZ equality criterion.
